articles.title: Grid-Orch: An LLM-Powered Orchestrator for Distribution Grid Simulation and Analytics
articles.summary: Grid-Orch is an LLM-powered framework that connects natural-language interfaces with power distribution simulation tools through the Model Context Protocol. Using OpenDSS, it supports 36 domain-specific tools for power flow, voltage analysis, QSTS simulation, and optimization, with both cloud-hosted and local model options for security-sensitive utility environments. Demonstrations show tasks such as DER interconnection screening moving from hours of scripting to under two minutes while matching direct OpenDSS results.
articles.advisor_relevance: This highlights a practical AI use case tied to grid modernization and utility labor constraints: using LLMs to make specialized engineering analysis faster and more accessible. While still presented as a research framework rather than a commercial deployment, it points to potential demand for AI-enabled software, secure local model deployment, and workflow automation in power infrastructure.

articles.title: AI in Science: Early Insights
articles.summary: A new arXiv paper analyzes AI use in science using 15 million Gemini interactions, an inventory of over 2,600 specialized AI models, and a survey of more than 600 scientists. The study also suggests AI is shifting research bottlenecks toward hypothesis testing and output verification.
